about: Poses for comic panels, written by hand as turns of our own 21 plain bones away from the T-pose. A turn is [x, y, z] in degrees about the character's own axes as it stands in the T-pose (it faces -y, +x is its left, z is up), carried along by the bones above it. A bone named without _l or _r means both sides, mirrored; write the left side. x+ leans or nods forward (a thigh: x- lifts it forward). y+ lowers the left arm. z- swings the left arm forward. After the turns the character is set down so its lowest point is on the floor.

stand.about: standing easy, arms at the sides

talk.about: standing, one hand raised palm-up while talking

point.about: pointing straight ahead with one arm

cheer.about: both arms thrown up in triumph

hands_on_hips.about: hands on hips, elbows out, sure of itself

shrug.about: a shrug: shoulders up, palms out to the sides

think.about: one hand at the chin, thinking

guard.about: a wrestler's ready stance: knees bent, leaning in, hands out in front

slump.about: shoulders dropped, head down, beaten or sad

laugh.about: leaning back with the arms folded over the belly, laughing or unimpressed

startled.about: jerked back in surprise, arms flung out

bow.about: a polite bow from the waist, arms at the sides
